intro: What broke, what we locked, and what earned a place on disk — filed when the week earns it.

posts.title: v1.0 — locked baseline
body: Enough shape to ship. The notebook has a finish line (60 minutes + Cursor pack), a brand, a cadence (EOW), and the operating sections that earned their keep.
v1.0.0 is the lock: don’t casually rewrite the public skeleton mid-week. Improve the pack, patterns, and notes when the week earned it. Cut v1.1 when the shape itself changes.
Release and baseline note live on GitHub. Steal the pack. Measure your own results.

posts.title: We update this at EOW
body: How often should a public notebook move? Daily posts are vanity. Never is rot.

We’ll update chopwoodcarrywater.uk in the end-of-week review — the same Hansei pass where patterns get keep / amend / retire. If the week earned a note, a pack tweak, or a pattern change, it ships then. If not, we skip. No filler calendar.
That’s the cadence: weekly with the review, not whenever a chat feels productive.

posts.title: Start in 60 minutes
body: A notebook full of patterns is useless if people only nod and leave. The useful finish line is a thin harness on disk.
There’s now a timed checklist and a downloadable Cursor pack: two always-on P0 rules, one skill to rename, one signed pattern, one clock. About an hour. Then stop for the day.
Come back for Toyota Way Practices and Preloop when the boring basics are already earning rent.

posts.title: Preloop + OpenRouter on PR commits
body: Desktop Preloop is one plane: tool policy and audit under Cursor’s human gates. The PR plane is different — and more useful when CI is scarce.

On product repos I wire a Preloop Cloud pull-request reviewer. OpenRouter is how that reviewer reaches models. Each push gets a GitHub commit status under context `preloop`. Actions can wait on that status before self-hosted jobs start, or leave the review async when I only want the signal.
It is not merge authority. It is not unit tests. It is shift-left: catch the semantic miss before the runner eats the afternoon. Keys stay vaulted. Humans still merge.

posts.title: Why this site is called chopwoodcarrywater.uk
body: There’s an old Zen line: before enlightenment, chop wood, carry water; after enlightenment, chop wood, carry water. We signed that off as a working pattern when the harness work started to feel shiny.

The temptation after a good insight is novelty — another skill, another abstraction, another brand. The useful move is usually the ordinary one: keep the sensors green, keep the gates honest, keep the always-on budget thin.
So when we needed a proper domain for this notebook, I didn’t want agent-something-ai.com. I wanted the proverb. The .com was taken; .uk was free. That felt right.

posts.title: Context is rent
body: Every always-on rule, fat skill, and optional tool server is paid on every turn. That’s not a metaphor — it’s the invoice.

We keep a lean core (memory, decisions, app control, a small durable runtime layer) and enable specialty tools only for the job. When the job ends, unload. No “leave it on in case”. Reloading the window is cheaper than carrying last week’s AppSec server forever.
If a session feels heavy, that’s a bug. Measure it. Cut it. The working relationship stays useful when the rent stays boring.

posts.title: Standard work, not lore
body: Chat is a terrible place to keep how you work. The next session won’t remember the clever aside, and the model will invent a confident substitute.

What stuck for us: when something actually works — or fails twice the same way — propose a thin pattern, get a human sign-off, encode it where agents will load it. Kaizen with teeth. Hansei when it hurts.
That’s why this notebook talks about skills, rules, and signed patterns instead of “prompts”. The model is powerful. The operating system around it is what makes Monday morning repeatable.
